key_insight: Steric and solvation control enables hybrid perovskite monolayers with lateral areas exceeding 1000 μm², supporting lithography-free, low-static-power optoelectronics.
engineering_relevance: Large ultrathin crystals enable solvent-free electrical contacts through physical shadow masks, avoiding solvent-induced degradation during conventional lithography.
method: Use a ternary-solvent growth strategy combining alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive to suppress out-of-plane stacking.
Tune alcohol chain length and solvent volatility to control precursor solvation and sustain edge-mediated transport during annealing.
Fabricate planar devices from isolated ultrathin (PEA)₂PbI₄ channels using physical shadow masking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports (PEA)₂CuCl₄ monolayer areas above 1000 μm² and (PEA)₂PbI₄ devices with dark currents of 10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹³ A, approximately 0.2 pW static power at 5 V, and a light-to-dark current ratio of 430.
watch_item: Wafer-scale coverage, device yield, and long-term operational stability are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
